changes.source:
The runner checks the tool versions, runs each tool separately, and records the
commands, input hashes, host, versions, and return codes in `run.json`.
`ruff.json` contains Ruff diagnostics; `mypy.txt` contains mypy's report. Each
tool also has a separate stderr file. Read both reports even if the first tool
finds a problem. Use a new output directory for each rerun; the runner refuses to
overwrite earlier reports. Setup failures are recorded in `run.json`, and a
timeout retains any partial output.
changes.replacement:
The runner verifies versions, runs each tool separately, and saves commands,
input hashes, host details, versions, and return codes in `run.json`. Diagnostics
go in `ruff.json` and `mypy.txt`, with separate stderr files. Read both reports.
Use a new output directory for each rerun; the runner refuses to overwrite
earlier reports. It records setup failures and retains partial output on timeout.
changes.reason: Combine repeated report descriptions without dropping version checks, separate outputs, overwrite protection, or failure evidence.

changes.source: For this small recipe, every reported diagnostic blocks the gate. For an existing project, introduce a reviewed rule set and scope, then decide whether existing findings need a tracked remediation period. Do not regenerate a baseline on every run to force a passing status.

changes.source:
The [pinned package metadata](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/1.1.407/packages/pyright/package.json)
and [CLI reference](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/main/docs/command-line.md)
describe installation requirements and invocation. This minimal file has no
third-party imports. For a real project, set the intended interpreter, platform,
dependencies, and stubs before interpreting missing-import diagnostics.

## Start with the project environment

Use the documented CLI installation and point Pyright at a small package. Configure the intended Python interpreter, target version, and import paths before interpreting missing-import or unknown-type messages. Choose a diagnostic mode deliberately and review its defaults.

The [pinned package metadata](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/1.1.407/packages/pyright/package.json)

describe installation requirements and invocation. This minimal file has no
third-party imports.
